caption: Blue paint is dabbed onto a wet patch of yellow watercolour, and the colours bleed into each other making green where they meet.

sa.check: A wet patch of yellow watercolour is on paper.
Blue paint is dabbed onto it.
The colours bleed into each other.
The dab comes first and the bleeding follows.

pc.expect: The green forms along the boundary and widens as the paint spreads; it does not retreat.
pc.fail: The green shrinks; or the colours separate again; or green appears where the paints have not met.

pc.expect: The mix is green, and the pure yellow and blue remain at the edges.
pc.fail: The mix is a colour other than green; or the pure colours change; or the whole patch turns one colour at once.

pc.expect: Wet watercolour bleeds and feathers on the paper.
pc.fail: It stays as hard-edged blobs; or beads up and rolls; or the paper stays dry.

pc.expect: The paint spreads only where wet and where dabbed.
pc.fail: It jumps across dry paper; or the paper moves; or the brush moves by itself.
The sheet duplicates; or the brush vanishes; or paint appears from nowhere.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The paper and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: The paper changes shape; or the table changes; or the brush changes.

note: The hand is the minimal trigger; the person is not judged.
